commentaryZh: 本章探讨了“道”无处不在的特征（小而无内，大而无外）及“道”化育万物、生养万物却不占有、不主宰万物的品德，即“生而不有，为而不恃，长而不宰”的玄德。大道无处不在，无所不及。天地万物都要依赖它生存、生长，但它从不推辞，它滋养万物，虽功高无比，但从不居功自傲而自居为万物的主人。这种无欲无求的奉献精神可以说是“道”的“小”吧。天地万物都主动归附于它，而它却不因此自诩为万物的主宰，这种精神可以说是“道”的“大”吧。正因为“道”不自认为伟大，所以才能成就它的伟大。
commentaryEn: This chapter discusses the nature and virtue of the Tao. It highlights that Tao is omnipresent. It is both infinitely small and infinitely great. And it also explains its mystic virtue that it generates and nurtures all things without possessing or dominating them. The Great Tao is present everywhere and reaches all things. All beings in heaven and earth depend on it for their existence and growth, yet it never refuses its role. It nourishes and sustains the myriad things, yet it never claims credit for his achievements or regards itself as the master of all things. This spirit of selfless giving, free from desire or demand, may be considered the Tao’s “smallness.” At the same time, all things under heaven naturally turn to and rely upon it, yet the Tao never proclaims itself the ruler of the myriad things. This spirit may be regarded as the Tao’s “greatness.” Precisely because the Tao does not consider itself great, it is able to achieve true greatness.

title: 仁德
original: 执大象天下往。往而不害安平太。乐与饵，过客止。道之出口淡乎其无味。视之不足见。听之不足闻。用之不足既。
translation: He who holds fast to the Great Tao attracts all the people under Heaven to him. With harmless interactions there will be peace, security and prosperity among all. Sweet music and delicious food can allure and halt passers-by. In contrast, the Tao is flavorless, invisible and inaudible. However, its usefulness remains inexhaustible.
commentaryZh:
本章论述了“道”的作用和影响以及“道”的“无味”、“看不见”和“听不到”等
特征。坚守大道的君王一定会赢得天下人心，人民都会主动归附他。百姓纷纷归顺而又不彼此伤害，那么天下就会安乐、安宁、太平，即国泰民安。统治阶层容易被声色犬马的物欲诱惑，如：听到美妙的音乐和见到美味的食物他们会停下脚步，流连忘返。相比之下，用语言表达出来的“道”的状态却相反：平淡无味、看不见、听不到，但它的作用却无穷无尽，绵延不绝。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi discusses the function and influence of the Tao, as well as its characteristics of being tasteless, invisible, and inaudible. A ruler who firmly upholds the Great Tao will surely win the hearts of the people, and they will willingly support him. When the people come towards him without harming one another, the world will enjoy peace, tranquility, and stability, and the state will flourish while the people live in security. The ruling class is easily tempted by pleasures and material desires. For example, when they hear beautiful music or see delicious food, they stop and linger, unable to leave. In contrast, the Tao as expressed in words appears plain and without flavor; it cannot be seen or heard. Yet its power and influence are inexhaustible and continue without end.

title: 微明
original: 将欲歙之，必固张之。将欲弱之，必固强之。将欲废之，必固兴之。将欲取之，必固与之。是谓微明。柔弱胜刚强。鱼不可脱於渊，国之利器不可以示人。
translation: He who intends to shrink something has to expand it first; He who intends to weaken something has to strengthen it first; He who intends to eradicate something has to make it prosper first; He who intends to take something has to give something first. This is subtle and profound wisdom. It proves true indeed that weakness will always conquer strength in the long term. Leaving deep water, a fish will die; The harsh and severe methods of governing the state should not be imposed upon the populace readily.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子详细论述了他的“以柔克刚”的哲学思想，阐释了事物两重性和矛盾相互转化的辩证关系。老子说：要想收缩一个东西，就必须先把它张开；要想削弱它，就必须先让它变强大；要想废掉它，就必须先使它兴盛；要想夺取它，就必须先给予它好处。这是微妙隐藏的智慧啊！柔弱的可以战胜强大的。鱼儿不能离开深水，因为那是它活下去的根本保障，离开水就必定干死。治理国家的利器，即统治者用以治理国家的严刑峻法不可以向世人炫耀和张扬，这一点折射了老子主张“无为而治”的核心思想。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi elaborates on his philosophy of "conquering the strong with the weak," and explains the duality of things and the transformation of opposites. He says: To shrink something, one must first expand it; to weaken it, one must first make it strong; to destroy it, one must first make it prosper; to take it, one must first give it benefits. This is the wisdom of acting in a subtle and concealed manner! The soft and weak can overcome the strong. Fish cannot live without water, for it is the fundamental guarantee of their survival. If removed from the water, they will surely die. Similarly, the effective tool for governing a nation, that is the ruler’s harsh and severe methods should not be exposed to the world. This reflects Laozi’s core idea of “governing through non-action”.

title: 为政
original: 道常无为，而无不为。侯王若能守之，万物将自化。化而欲作，吾将镇之以无名之朴。无名之朴，夫亦将无欲。不欲以静，天下将自定。
translation: The Tao always acts naturally and leaves us an impression that it does nothing; Yet it turns out that nothing is left undone. If rulers follow the Tao, the myriad things will grow and flourish of their own accord. Once people's desires arise in their growth process, I would curb them by virtue of the nameless simplicity (the Tao) . Through the Tao, people will be freed of selfish desires and enjoy quietude.That being the case, peace and prosperity will naturally prevail in the world.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子论述了“道”的规律：无所作为而又无所不为，即“无为而无不为”。“道”永远顺其自然，不妄为，即“道”的“无为”，而天下万事万物没有一个不遵循“道”而生存和运行，这就是“道”的“无不为”。君王如果能坚守“道”的规律去治理天下，那么天下百姓也会按照“道”的规律繁衍生息、自然生灭。一旦有君王在此过程中产生了多余的贪欲，想有所“妄为”，我就利用质朴的“道”来制服他。这样一来，私欲就不会再出来作怪了。没有了私欲作怪，人们自然就清净而淡泊名利了。“无为”将流行于天下，百姓自然会过上安定、稳定、祥和的 生活。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi discusses the principle of the Tao: it does nothing, yet there is nothing it does not accomplish, that is “non-action, yet nothing left undone”. The Tao always follows its own natural course and never acts arbitrarily, and this is what is meant by non-action. At the same time, everything in the world exists and grows in accordance with the Tao, and this is what is meant by nothing left undone. If rulers can adhere to the principle of the Tao in their governance, the people will likewise live in accordance with it. Should a ruler develop excessive desires and attempt to act willfully, the simplicity of the Tao can be used to restrain such impulses. In this way, selfish desires will no longer arise. In this way, his people will naturally become simple and indifferent to fame and profit. Non-action will prevail throughout the world, and the people will naturally live peaceful, stable, and harmonious lives.

title: 论德
original: 上德不德是以有德。下德不失德是以无德。上德无为而无以为。下德无为而有以为。上仁为之而无以为。上义为之而有以为。上礼为之而莫之以应，则攘臂而扔之。故失道而後德。失德而後仁。失仁而後义。失义而後礼。夫礼者忠信之薄而乱之首。前识者，道之华而愚之始。是以大丈夫，处其厚不居其薄。处其实，不居其华。故去彼取此。
translation: A man of superior virtue does not claim to be virtuous and is therefore virtuous indeed; A man of inferior virtue holds fast to virtue in form and is therefore not virtuousindeed. A man of superior virtue acts naturally but not out of his own interest; A man of inferior virtue acts intentionally but out of his own interest; A man of superior benevolence acts spontaneously but without any personal intention; A man of superior righteousness acts vigorously but with intention; A man of superior propriety acts purposefully, but if ignored, he rolls up his sleeves to compel others to respond to his actions. Therefore: With the loss of the Tao, arose the concept of virtue; With the loss of virtue, arose the concept of benevolence; With the loss of benevolence, arose the concept of righteousness; With the loss of righteousness, arose the concept of propriety. Propriety becomes necessary owing to the decline of loyalty and trustworthiness; From propriety comes great disorder as well. Prophetic knowledge proves nothing but the flowery decoration of the Tao, which turns out to become the source of foolishness and ignorance. Therefore: A ruler chooses to cherish the fundamental rather than the superficial, and value the fruit rather than the flower. He discards the latter and takes the former.
commentaryZh:
本章是《道德经》的“德篇”的第一章，是老子对“德”论述的核心思想，老子认为“德”是“道”的最根本属性，化“道”于“德”就是“悟道”的最关键的过程，即：“道”为宇宙万物的客观规律，而“德”是人类认识这些规律并用于指导自己的社会实践的能力。有这种能力的人就是有德之人，反之就是无德之人。老子把“德”划分为“上德”和“下德”。上德之人尽管有德，但不自居有德，这样的德才是至高的德。下德之人自认为有德，故在形式上表现出自己有德或不离开德，这种行为实际上是没有德的表现。上德之人尊“道”而行“无为”之事，他们顺应“大道”，自然无心故意作为；下德之人总是想做些事情，但有意作为，带有自私的欲念。老子认为好的政治体制应该是以“道”和“德”为基础的“无为”的那种类型，而建立在“仁、义、礼”基础上的政治体制属于“有为”的类型，因为这种政
治体制有浓厚的人为色彩，是“道”与“德”失去后人为的政治体制。老子说：最上等的仁是有所作为但完全出于无意，不是为了留名或出名；最有义的人做事都完全出于目的或有意而为；最有礼的人做事完全出于目的或有意而为，如果他们的作为得不到别人的积极回应，他们就会举起胳膊强行拉着别人跟他们去行动。所以，道理就清楚了：失去了道才提倡德，失去了德才提倡仁，失去了仁才提倡义，失去了义才提倡礼。所以，礼是忠信匮乏的产物，是人心大乱和社会动荡的开始。所谓先知灼见只不过是“道”的华丽外表，是愚昧无知的发端。所以，君王要为人厚重淳朴而不要轻薄浮华。
commentaryEn: This chapter is the first chapter of the De section of Tao Te Ching and presents Laozi’s central ideas on De (virtue). Laozi holds that virtue is the most fundamental attribute of the Tao. Transforming the Tao into virtue is the key process of realizing the Tao. In other words, the Tao represents the objective laws governing all things in the universe, while virtue refers to the capacity to understand these laws and apply them to real life. Those who possess this capacity are people of virtue; those who do not are without it. Laozi further distinguishes between “higher virtue” and “lower virtue.” A person of higher virtue possesses virtue yet does not regard himself as virtuous; only such virtue can be considered the highest form of virtue. A person of lower De believes himself to be virtuous and therefore consciously displays virtue. Such behavior, in fact, reveals the absence of true virtue. Those of higher virtue honors the Tao and practice non-action. They follow the Great Tao and act naturally, without deliberate intention. Those of lower De, by contrast, always seek to act and do so intentionally, driven by self-centered desires. Laozi believes that an ideal governance should be founded upon the principles of the Tao and virtue and characterized by non-action. Yet those based on benevolence, righteousness, and ritual belong to the realm of deliberate action, for they bear a strong human interference and arise only after the Tao and virtue have been lost. Laozi further explains that the highest form of benevolence acts, yet without conscious intention and not for the sake of reputation or fame. Those who practice righteousness act with clear purpose and intention. Those who uphold ritual also act intentionally; if others fail to respond positively to their actions, they may even raise their arms and forcibly compel others to follow them. From this the principle becomes clear: when the Tao is lost, virtue is advocated; when virtue is lost, benevolence is advocated; when benevolence is lost, righteousness is advocated; and when righteousness is lost, ritual propriety is advocated. Ritual, therefore, is the product of the decline of loyalty and trust and marks the beginning of social disorder. What is called foresight is merely the superficial aspect of the Tao and the starting point of ignorance. For this reason, rulers should value sincerity, simplicity, and solidity rather than superficial brilliance and ostentation.

title: 法本
original: 昔之得一者。天得一以清。地得一以宁。神得一以灵。谷得一以盈。万物得一以生。侯王得一以为天下贞。其致之。天无以清将恐裂。地无以宁将恐废。神无以灵将恐歇。谷无以盈将恐竭。万物无以生将恐灭。侯王无以贞将恐蹶。故贵以贱为本，高以下为基。是以侯王自称孤、寡、不谷。此非以贱为本邪？非乎。至誉无誉。不欲琭琭如玉，珞珞如石。
translation: In ancient times what happened to those followers of the Tao is as follows: By embracing the Tao, Heaven became clear; By embracing the Tao, Earth became stable; By embracing the Tao, spirits were able to display their spirituality; By embracing the Tao, valleys became full; By embracing the Tao, the myriad things came to life; By embracing the Tao, rulers could head the world. What would happen if they did not follow the Tao? Without being clear, Heaven would crack wide open; Without being stable, Earth would collapse; W ithout spirituality, spirits would lose their spiritual power; Without being full, valleys would go dry; W ithout life-giving power, the myriad things would go extinct; Without being able to head the world, rulers would be overthrown. Therefore: The noble must depend on the common for support; The high must take the low as its foundation. That's why rulers choose to call themselves “"the orphaned", "the lonely” and "the unworthy". This is taking humility as the foundation, isn't it? Thus, the best praise is no praise. A ruler should not pursue valuable objects like jade, beautiful clothes, and magnificent palaces, etc, instead he should pay much heed to such solid qualities as simplicity, honesty, reliability and trustworthiness, etc.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子用诗一般的语言从正反两个方面论述了“道”的作用。天地万物都来源于“道”，它是宇宙的原创力。不失或遵循“道”，宇宙万物（天、地、神、谷、万物、统治者等）生生不息；如果失去了“道”，那么宇宙万物就会崩溃、消亡。接着，老子由此推及统治者并警告他们必须尊“道”贵“德”，践行“贵以贱为本”和“高以下为基”的“处下、居后、谦卑”的治国理政的基本原则，也就是“守道”的原则。其实，“贱”与“下”也指“人民、天下百姓”。统治者只有把处于低位的天下百姓当作其统治的根基，他们的高贵才能被凸显，天下才能“安平泰”。百姓的安定富足和社会的和谐稳定才是给予统治者最高的荣誉，这是任何溢美之词所不能比拟的。统治者应遵循这个原则，不要贪求看上去华丽、昂贵的东西，如晶莹的美玉，而应追求朴实、坚固的东西，如坚硬的石头。前者代表了“贵”，而后者代表了“贱”。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi employs beautiful language to explain the function of the Tao from both positive and negative perspectives. All things in heaven and earth originate from the Tao, which serves as the creative source of the universe. When the Tao is preserved and followed, all things in the universe—heaven, earth, spirits, valleys, the myriad beings, and rulers—will flourish. If the Tao is lost, the myriad things  will collapse and perish. Laozi then extends this principle to rulers, warning them that they must honor the Tao and value virtue. They should “depend on the common for support” and “must take the low as its foundation”, which emphasize humility, placing oneself behind others, and dwelling in a lower position. These principles constitute the essence of the Tao. In fact, “the common” and “the low” also refer to the common populace under heaven. Only when rulers regard the common people as the foundation of their rule can their own nobility be manifested and the world remain peaceful and stable. The well-being and prosperity of the people, together with social harmony and stability, represent the highest honor that can be bestowed upon rulers—far surpassing any words of praise. Therefore, rulers should rather than seeking precious things, like shining jade, they should value plain and solid things, like hard stone. The former symbolizes the noble and precious, while the latter represents the humble and lowly.

title: 去用
original: 反者道之动。弱者道之用。天下万物生於有，有生於无。
translation: Cycling is the movement of the Tao; Being weak and humble is the function of the Tao. The myriad things are born from Being, and Being comes from Nothingness.
commentaryZh: 本章是《道德经》中很著名的一章，人们常说的“反动”一词就来自本章。在这一章中，老子简明扼要地论述了“道”的规律和作用。“道”的运动规律是循环往复或向着相反的方向发展，即“事物的矛盾和对立转化是永恒不变的规律”。 “道”的作用体现在“柔弱”上，其表现方式包含“柔弱、顺从、谦卑、处下、安静、无为、不争”等等。总之，循环往复或向相反的方向发展，就是“道”运动的自然规律；显示微妙柔弱是“道”的作用。天下万物都生于有形的物质，而有形的物质 又生于无形的物质。本章再次提到“有”与“无”的关系。
commentaryEn: This chapter is one of the most well-known chapters in Tao Te Ching. The commonly used expression “reversal” is often traced back to this chapter. Here, Laozi explains the pattern and function of Tao. The movement of the Tao follows a pattern of cyclical return or development toward the opposite direction. In other words, the transformation of opposites is a universal principle governing all things. The function of the Tao is manifested in softness and weakness, expressed through qualities such as gentleness, compliance, humility, lowliness, stillness, non-action, and non-contention. In short, cyclical return or movement toward the opposite direction is the natural law of the Tao’s operation, while subtle softness and weakness is the function of it. All things under heaven arise from tangible forms, while tangible materials themselves emerge from what is intangible. In this chapter, the relationship between “being” and “nothingness” is once again emphasized.

title: 同异
original: 上士闻道勤而行之。中士闻道若存若亡。下士闻道大笑之。不笑不足以为道。故建言有之。明道若昧。进道若退。夷道若纇。上德若谷。大白若辱。广德若不足。建德若偷。质真若渝。大方无隅。大器晚成。大音希声。大象无形。道隐无名。夫唯道善贷且成。
translation: Hearing of the Tao, a superior scholar tries his utmost to put it into practice; Hearing of the Tao, a mediocre scholar half believes and half doubts it; Hearing of the Tao, an inferior scholar laughs out loud at it. If it were not laughed at, it would not be the Tao. As the ancients put it: The bright Tao appears dim; The advancing Tao appears to be slipping back; The even Tao appears uneven; The highest virtue resembles a deep valley; The purest white appears tainted; Abundant virtue appears insufficient; Vigorous virtue appears idle; The greatest purity appears sullied; The largest square seems to have no corners; A great talent takes long to come into maturity; The loudest sound can't be heard; The largest form can't be seen. The Tao is nameless and invisible. It is the Tao alone that creates the myriad things and matures them.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子描述了不同等级的士对“闻道”的不同态度与反应。上等智慧的士听到了“道”就会努力去践行；中等智慧的士听到了“道”会半信半疑，对于是否践行犹豫不决；下等智慧的士听到了“道”会对其哈哈大笑来冷嘲热讽。对于这种嘲讽，老子自我解嘲说：如果不被这样的人嘲笑，那还是真正的“道”吗？接着老子借用古人之口以排山倒海的排比句式列举了十二对看似相互矛盾的成语或短句以突出他所要强调的思想：任何事物的内部都存在着一对既对立又统一、既排斥又相互依赖的矛盾体。其实，这对矛盾就是“一阴一阳”的存在。这生动地体现了老子的对立统一的辩证法哲学思想。同时，老子也强调了悟道者要体悟“道”的“昧、退、纇、谷、辱、不足、偷、渝、无隅、晚成、希声、无形、无名”等特征之后方能修成大道。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi describes how scholars of different levels respond when they hear about Tao. Those of the highest wisdom strive to practice Tao when they hear about it. Those of mediocre wisdom were suspicious of Tao. Those of the lowest wisdom laugh at it with ridicule when they hear of it. Laozi ironically remarks that if the Tao were not laughed at by such people, it would hardly be the true Tao. He then, in the voice of the ancients, presents twelve seemingly contradictory parallel expressions. Through these contrasts, Laozi emphasizes that within all things there exists a pair of opposing yet unified forces that both resist and depend upon one another. In essence, this contradiction reflects the coexistence of yin and yang. This also illustrates Laozi’s dialectical philosophy of the unity of opposites. At the same time, Laozi stresses that to understand the Tao, one must grasp its  characteristics, such as obscurity, retreat, imperfection, humility, disgrace, insufficiency, subtle change, the absence of corners, late maturity, faint sound, formlessness, and namelessness.

title: 道化
original: 道生一。一生二。二生三。三生万物。万物负阴而抱阳，冲气以为和。人之所恶，唯孤、寡不谷，而王公以为称，故物或损之而益，或益之而损。人之所教，我亦教之，强梁者，不得其死。吾将以为教父。
translation: The Tao is the underlying force called One that creates all things under Heaven; It gives birth to two generative forces: the Yin and the Yang; With the interaction of the Yin and the Yang the myriad things are created.The myriad things have their backs to the Yin and face the Yang;Through the dynamic union of the Yin and the Yang, a new harmony is created. People hate such words as "the orphaned", "the lonely", and "the unworthy". Yet rulers choose to address themselves humbly by these names. Why? To diminish something is to increase it, and vice versa. I will also teach the teachings of the sages: The violent man shall not die a natural death. I shall take this as the essence of my teaching.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子首先论述了“道”的基本内涵及“道”化育万物的过程，本章与第一章遥相呼应。“道”就是由“一”构成的独一无二的统一体，“一”包含“二”， “二”就是“阴”和“阳”二气，即《易经》中的“一阴一阳之谓道”中的阴阳。阴阳也可以指“天地”。阴阳二气交合、互动激荡就生成了“三”，即万物。“道”的本质就是使万物“生”，即生生不息。万物都是背阴向阳并在阴阳二气的参与、交合、互动、磨合、激荡与交融中生成新的、和谐的事物。阴阳的对立统一是万物化育的最根本原动力，就是“道”的规律。这也是老子辩证法思想的核心内涵。紧接着，老子说世人都厌恶“孤、寡、不谷”这些称呼，而王侯却喜欢用这些来称呼自己，为什么呢？其实，这正体现了“道”的“阴阳平衡”的规律，是“阴而向阳”的人生态度，用“阴”的状态提醒“阳”的状态。涉及为人处世，就是身处高位的人要不断提醒自己处下、低调、谦卑、谦虚等。借此，老子又归纳出一条符合“天道” 的“人道”：物或损之而益，或益之而损。老子认为世上万事万物，如果你减损它反而会增益它，如果你执意增益它反而会减损它。这句话内涵就是“祸兮福之所倚，福兮祸之所伏”。遵循“阴阳平衡”就是尊“道”，“守柔处下”就是贵“道”。所以，老子说：逞强好胜的人不得好死。我要把它当成我教人的根本原则。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi first expounds the fundamental meaning of the Tao and the process by which it gives rise to all things, echoing the opening chapter. The Tao is described as the unique and unified “One.” Within the One is contained the “Two,” namely yin and yang. These two forces are described in the I Ching as constituting the Tao. They can also be understood as heaven and earth. Through their interaction and alternation, the “Three” emerges and the myriad things are generated. The essential nature of the Tao lies in generating life. All beings turn away from yin and toward yang, and through integrating into the interaction of yin and yang, new and harmonious forms arise. The unity of opposites is thus the fundamental driving force behind all things, and this is also the principle of Tao, which is the core of Laozi’s dialectical thought. Laozi then observes that people generally dislike words like “orphaned,” “destitute,” or “unworthy,” yet rulers often use such terms to refer to themselves. Why? This practice reflects the Tao’s principle of balancing yin and yang and an attitude of standing against yin and facing Yang, using what is “low” to check what is “high.” Applied to conduct, it means that those in power must continually remind themselves to remain modest and humble. From this, Laozi formulates a principle that aligns the Tao of heaven: sometimes loss brings gain, and sometimes gain brings loss. If one deliberately diminishes something, it may in fact flourish; if one insists on increasing it, it may decline. This echoes the idea that misfortune rests upon fortune, and fortune conceals misfortune. To maintain the balance of yin and yang is to honor the Tao; to practice softness and humility is to value it. Hence Laozi warns that those who are aggressive and overly competitive will not meet a good end. He presents as the foundation of his teaching.

title: 遍用
original: 天下之至柔，驰骋天下之至坚。无有入无间，吾是以知无为之有益。不言之教，无为之益天下希及之。
translation: The softest substance under Heaven can go through the hardest substance in the world. The shapeless substance can penetrate the solid substance that has no crevices. Through this I get to know the benefits of non-interference. Rulers can rarely understand the principle of teaching without words and the benefits of non-action, let alone achieve them.
commentaryZh: 本章重点探讨了老子的“以柔克刚”的思想。“守柔”是老子哲学的根基，这体现了老子“道法自然”“无为而治”的政治理念。能体现天下最柔弱特性的物质就是水，而水却能攻击、贯穿天下最坚硬的东西，如金石（水滴石穿）。无形的力量可以穿透任何没有空隙的物体（热量、电磁波、射线等可以在任何坚硬物体的缝隙间自由驰骋）。老子说他因此明白了“无为”确实有好处。不乱发号施令，“无为”带来的好处，天下很少有人（如君王）能领悟这个道理并将其付诸实践。
commentaryEn: This chapter centers on Laozi’s principle of “the soft can overcome the hard.” To “abide in softness” forms the foundation of his philosophy and reflects his political vision of following what is natural and governing through non-action. Water is the softest thing in the world, through its persistent flow, it can attack and penetrate the hardest substances, such as metal and stone. In the same way, intangible forces, such as subtle energies, can pass through solid matter which seem impenetrable. From this, Laozi concludes that non-action truly has its advantages. By refraining from arbitrary commands and excessive interference, a ruler allows natural processes to unfold. Yet few in the world, especially those in power, are able to grasp and practice this principle.

title: 立戒
original: 名与身孰亲。身与货孰多。得与亡孰病。是故甚爱必大费。多藏必厚亡。知足不辱。知止不殆。可以长久。
translation: Which do you hold more dear, fame or life? Which do you value more, life or wealth? Which do you think is more harmful, gaining fame and fortune or losing your life? Therefore: You have to pay more in your over-greedy seeking fame and fortune; You are doomed to suffer heavier losses if you hoard more wealth. Being content with what you already have will incur no disgrace; Knowing when to stop will bring you no danger; By doing so, you endure.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子以三连问的句式追问了生命的意义，震耳欲聋，发人深省。名声与生命相比，哪个更值得珍惜？生命与财货相比，哪个更重要？得到名利 与失去生命，哪个更有害？所以，过分追逐名利必然要付出巨大代价；过多积敛 财富必然招来更大的损失。知道满足就不会招来耻辱（知足常乐），懂得该止的 时候要止（适可而止）就不会招致危险，只有这样，一个人（尤其是统治者）才能长久平安、稳定。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi employs a series of probing rhetorical questions to confront the meaning of life. His questions are profound and thought-provoking. Which is more important, reputation or life itself? Which is more important, life or material wealth? And which is more harmful, gaining fame and wealth, or losing one’s life? From these questions follows a clear warning: excessive pursuit of reputation and wealth inevitably costs a heavy price; over accumulation of wealth brings even greater loss. One who knows contentment avoids disgrace, and one who knows when to stop avoids danger. Only in this way can a person, especially a ruler, secure lasting peace and stability.

title: 洪德
original: 大成若缺，其用不弊。大盈若冲，其用不穷。大直若屈。大巧若拙。大辩若讷。静胜躁，寒胜热。清静为天下正。
translation: The most perfect thing seems to be somewhat imperfect, yet its function never fails. The fullest thing seems to be somewhat empty, yet its use cannot be exhausted." The straightest thing appears somewhat bent; The most skillful thing seems somewhat clumsy; The most eloquent person seems to be somewhat tongue-tied. Movement conquers cold; Quietude overcomes heat; By exercising tranquil non-action, one is qualified to be the head of a country.
commentaryZh: 本章体现了老子的辩证思想，突出他“万物忌满”的思想，而这就是“天道忌满”的“道”的精神。天下最完美的东西（道）好像有点瑕疵，但它的作用却永不枯竭；最盈满或充实的东西好像有些虚空，但它的作用却无穷无尽；天下最笔直的东西好像有些弯曲，最灵巧的东西好像有点笨拙，最擅长辩论的人好像有点不善言说。躁动或运动可以抵御严寒，安静下来燥热就会消失。（君王）若能达到清静无为的境界就可以治理天下、号令天下了。在本章中，“大成、大盈、大直、大巧、大辩”等都属于“道”的内在本质范畴，而那些看上去不足之处，如“若缺、若冲、若屈、若拙、若讷”是“道”的外在表现特征，也是“道”之“弱”的妙用。
commentaryEn: In this chapter. Laozi explains his dialectical thought that “all things should avoid excess”. This echos with the spirit of the Tao itself, which likewise shuns fullness. The most perfect thing under heaven, the Tao, may appear flawed, yet its function never fails. The fullest thing may appear empty, yet its usefulness is inexhaustible. The straightest thing appears bent. The most skillful things seems clumsy and the most eloquent person appears hesitant in speech. Movement dispels the cold, while stillness overcomes heat. If a ruler can attain a state of , tranquility and non-action, he is capable of governing the world. In this chapter, “great perfection,” “great fullness,” “great straightness,” “great skill,” and “great eloquence” refer to the characteristic of the Tao. By contrast, the seemingly deficient qualities, “somewhat flawed,” “somewhat empty,” “somewhat bent,” “somewhat clumsy,” “somewhat tongue-tied” describe its outward manifestations. These weaknesses are, in fact, the subtle and powerful workings of the Tao’s softness.

title: 俭欲
original: 天下有道，却走马以粪。天下无道，戎马生於郊。祸莫大於不知足。咎莫大於欲得。故知足之足常足矣。
translation: When the Tao prevails in the world, battle steeds are returned to farmers for tilling the fields. When the Tao fails to prevail in the world, even pregnant mares are taken over for wars and colts are bred on the battlefields. Nothing is more disastrous than extreme desires; No crime is greater than greediness. Therefore: He who understands the contentment derived from being content enjoys eternal contentment.
commentaryZh: 本章体现了老子的反战思想。他一针见血地指出统治阶级发动战争的主要原因就是永不知足的贪婪欲望。如果天下行“无为”之道，那么战马就不用上战场了，就可以把战马退还给农夫用来耕种田地了；如果天下行“有为”之事，统治阶级就会为了满足自己的私欲而不顾天下苍生之疾苦，贸然发动战争，就连怀孕的母马也被征用上了战场，以至于母马在战场上产崽。贪得无厌是世上最大的祸根与罪恶之源。懂得知足带来的富足之感才是永恒的富足。
commentaryEn: This chapter reflects the anti-war thought of Laozi. He points out that the primary cause of war lies in the greed of those in power. If non-action prevails under heaven, warhorses will no longer be sent to the battlefield but will be returned to the fields to plow the land. By contrast, when the Tao fails to prevail, rulers disregard the suffering of the people and recklessly initiate wars to satisfy their private ambitions. In such times, even pregnant mares are sent to war and forced to give birth amid the chaos. Greed is thus the greatest source of calamity and wrongdoing in the world, whereas contentment brings enduring wealth.

title: 鉴远
original: 不出户知天下。不窥牖见天道。其出弥远，其知弥少。是以圣人不行而知。不见而明。不为而成。
translation: He who follows the Tao is able to understand the principles underlying all things without stepping out of the door; He who follows the Tao is able to comprehend the Tao of Heaven without looking out of the window. The more knowledge he pursues, the less wisdom he acquires. Therefore: The sage gets to know the Tao without journeying; He gets to understand the Tao without observing the outside world; He accomplishes much by doing nothing against the Tao.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子谈到“悟道”的关键是内省、内观。在心灵清明觉醒的过程中不断接近和洞察“道”的规律，而不是唤起人的外求欲望或不断地求知来达到 “悟道”的目的。如果“道”能学会或被教会，那学到的一定不是真的“道”，只不过是“道”的皮毛而已。所以，老子说，懂“道”的人不用出门外寻就能推知天下事理。他不是闷在家里胡思乱想，而是能从细小之处推知更接近“道”的原理，不用往窗外看就可以理解自然万物的运行规律。一个人走出去越远或外求的知识越多，其知道的关于“道”的东西就越少。人的外求欲望越大，那么阻碍他 “悟道”的阻力就越大，他的心灵就离“道”越远。正如庄子所说，“其嗜欲深者，其天机浅”，“凡外重者，内拙”。所以有道之人（统治者）不必亲自出行或外出，就能对外界事物了如指掌，正所谓运筹帷幄之中而决胜千里之外；不用身体力行地观察，就能对天下万事万物的规律明察秋毫；不去妄为反而成就了许多利国利民的大事。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi explains that the key to understanding the Tao lies in inward reflection and inner illumination. Understanding the Tao does not come from stimulating desires or accumulating knowledge. Rather, it is through clarifying the mind that one gradually approaches and perceives the underlying patterns of the Tao. If the Tao could simply be learned or taught as ordinary knowledge, then that is not the true Tao, but only some superficial aspects. Thus Laozi suggests that one who understands the Tao need not go out to grasp the principles governing the world. This does not mean random speculation, but the ability to discern universal patterns from subtle details. The farther one travels in search of knowledge, the less one knows about the Tao. The stronger one’s desires are, the more difficult it becomes to get close to Tao. As Zhuangzi remarked, “The more desires one have, the less wisdom he has,” and “Those who are overly concerned with externals are inwardly poor”. Therefore, a ruler who embodies the Tao knows all things under heaven without traveling far. He understands the patterns of all things without excessive observation. He accomplishes much for his country and people through non-action.

title: 忘知
original: 为学日益。为道日损。损之又损，以至於无为。无为而不为。取天下常以无事，及其有事，不足以取天下。
translation: Pursuing worldly knowledge, one will experience a daily increase of his selfish desires; Yet pursuing the Tao, one will experience a daily decrease of his selfish desires. Through decreasing one' s selfish desires constantly, one can reach the state of non-action, in which nothing is left undone. If a ruler can govern his country through non-action, he will make it in hisgovernance. If he interferes too much in his people' s affairs, he is surely not qualified to govern his country.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子继续探讨“悟道”的途径，即“悟道”与外在的追求知识不一 样，“悟道”是需要不断减损自己的外求欲望。“悟道”的核心是“损”，就是做减法，尽可能地少私寡欲，最后达到“无为”的境界。而求知是每天都提升自己的知识量，其核心是“益”，其目的是提升人对自然的认知和干预的能力，就是做加法，也就是增加“有为”的能力，这与“悟道”的途径正好相反。只有“损之又损” 方能达到“无为”而“无不为”之境界。如果统治者能以“无为”取天下，则天下太平祥和，百姓悠然自得，反之，他就不配治理天下了。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi continues to explore how to pursue the Tao. He explains that pursuing the Tao differs fundamentally from the outward pursuit of knowledge. To realize the Tao requires a continual reduction of one’s external cravings. The essence of such realization lies in “subtraction”, that is to diminish selfish desires until one reaches the state of non-action. By contrast, the pursuit of knowledge operates through “addition”. It seeks daily accumulation, increasing one’s understanding of and control over the natural world. In this sense, it enhances the ability for deliberate action, which stands in direct contrast to non-action. Only through reducing and reducing again can one arrive at the condition of non-action, wherein nothing is left undone. If a ruler practices non-action in his governance, the world will be peaceful and harmonious, and the people will live calmly and contentedly. Otherwise, he is not qualified to govern under heaven.

title: 任德
original: 圣人无常心。以百姓心为心。善者吾善之。不善者吾亦善之，德善。信者吾信之。不信者吾亦信之，德信。圣人在天下，歙歙(xīxī,无所偏执的样子)焉，为天下浑其心。百姓皆注其耳目，圣人皆孩之。
translation: The sage has no fixed personal will ; Yet he takes the people's will as his own. He treats the good and the bad alike with a good heart; In this way, the good virtue in the people will be cultivated. He treats the trustworthy and the untrustworthy alike with a good heart; In this way, the trustworthiness in the people will be cultivated. He governs his country by curbing his personal desires, which makes the people simple and honest. When the people are all eyes and ears, paying close heed to the sage's words and actions, he treats them equally, restoring them to the innocent and simple state of infancy.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子描述了他心目中理想的有道的统治者的形象。他没有自己的私心并以百姓的意志（或民意）作为自己的意志和准则以顺应自然与大道。他对待依道而行的人和背离道而行的人的态度不偏不倚，一视同仁，都同样给予平等的善待。这样就会使人人向善、得善了，即“得道”了。对待诚实守信（信守道）和言而无信（不信守道）的人来说，他都选择同样信任，这样就会使人人的品德趋向诚实守信。有道之人在治理天下的过程中会极力收敛自己的私欲，行“无为”之治，使社会安详和合，教化百姓的思想回归混沌、敦厚的状态。天下百姓都关注圣人的言行举止，因为他是天下的领袖与表率。他会以“无为”之治使百姓的思想回归到婴儿的淳朴和天真自然的状态，这样，天下就会太平和谐了。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi portrays his vision of the ideal ruler—one who follows the Tao. Such a ruler has no will of his own but takes the will of the people as his own, thereby acting in harmony with the Tao. He treats those who follow the Tao and those who do not alike, without discrimination, as a result, people gradually turn toward goodness and follow the Tao. Likewise, he trusts both those who are trustworthy and those who are not, as a result, people become honest and trustworthy. In governing the country, a virtuous ruler restrains his personal desires and practices non-action, as a result, society becomes harmonious and stable, and the people become simple and sincere. Because he stands as a model for all under heaven, the people observe his conduct closely. Through non-action, he guides them back to childlike qualities of purity and sincerity. In this way, peace and harmony prevail throughout the world.

title: 贵生
original: 出生入死。生之徒，十有三。死之徒，十有三。人之生，动之於死地，亦十有三。夫何故？以其生生之厚。盖闻善摄生者，陆行不遇凶虎，入军不被甲兵。凶无所投其角。虎无所用其爪。兵无所容其刃。夫何故？以其无死地。
translation: From birth to death: Three out of ten people enjoy a long life; Three out of ten people die young; Three out of ten people could have enjoyed a longer life, yet die earlier because of their own highly motivated choices. Why is this? They are so eager to live longer that they over-nourish themselves, which leads to shortening their lives that should have been long. It has been said that one who knows well how to nurture life will be unhurt by the rhinos and tigers while traveling on land; He can also go through a battlefield unwounded. A rhino cannot use its deadly horn to pierce him; A tiger cannot use its sharp claws to harm him; The sharp edges of weapons cannot cut him. Why is this? Such a man who knows well how to nurture life will never put himself in a risky situation because he can foresee and mitigate perils.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子论述了“生死”及养生（或“贵生”）问题。他认为，从生到死，长寿者占十分之三；短命或夭折的人占十分之三；生下来本来可以活得久一些，但由于自己的原因而短命的人占十分之三。这是为什么呢？由于他们过于求长寿而营养过剩，最终因享受过度而过早死亡。剩下的人属于会养生的一类人。他们少私寡欲、恬淡从容、清净质朴的自然生活方式使他们延年益寿。老子在这里把使人折寿的欲望比喻成“兕、虎、甲兵”等凶猛的野兽和锋利的兵器，突出人的欲望是多么凶猛和有害，对于“养生”来说是最致命的威胁。为什么真正懂得“养生”的人不会受到“兕、虎、甲兵”的伤害和威胁呢？原因就是这样的人身上没有诱使其进入死亡或危险境地的致命弱点啊！正如孟子所认为：君子不立于危墙之下。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi discusses life and death, as well as the art of nurturing life. He observes that among those who live from birth to death, roughly three in ten are long-lived, three in ten die young or prematurely, and three in ten could have lived longer but shorten their lives through their own actions. Why does this happen? Because in their pursuit of longevity they indulge excessively, over-nourishing the body, thereby hastening their own decline. The remaining group are those who truly know how to care for life. With few selfish desires, a calm and contented spirit, and a simple, natural way of living, they are able to extend their years. Laozi vividly compares selfish desires to beasts and sharp weapons—rhinoceroses, tigers, and armored soldiers—emphasizing how dangerous and harmful selfish desires can be. For the cultivation of life, such desires are the most serious threat. Why, then, are those who truly understand how to nurture life free from these dangers? Because they have no fatal weakness that would draw them into peril or destruction. As Mencius likewise observed, the virtuous person does not place himself beneath a crumbling wall.

title: 养德
original: 道生之，德畜之，物形之，势成之。是以万物莫不尊道，而贵德。道之尊，德之贵，夫莫之命而常自然。故道生之，德畜之。长之育之。亭之毒之。养之覆之。生而不有，为而不恃，长而不宰。是谓玄德。
translation: The Tao gives birth to the myriad things, and virtue nurtures them; The material world that surrounds them makes them take different shapes and sizes, and the environment they live in brings them to maturity. That's why the myriad things esteem the Tao and value virtue. The reason why the Tao is worshiped and virtue is prized is that they do not interfere with the myriad things but always allow them to grow naturally. Therefore: The Tao gives birth to the myriad things, and virtue nurtures them, allows them to grow, nourishes them, brings them to maturity, and protects them. The Tao gives birth to the myriad things, yet it never claims its ownership; It benefits them, yet never boasts about it; It heads them, yet never dominates them; This is called "mystic virtue"
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子提出“尊道贵德”的思想并论述了何为“玄德”（上德）。“道”生化万物，而“德”养育万物。如果“道”是生成万物的先天因素，那么“德”就是后天养育呵护万物的力量和保障。有了“道”和“德”的“生”与“养”，它们还为万物提供了必要的物质条件和外部环境等来确保它们的成长和成熟，故有“物形之，势成之”的说法，所以，万物没有不尊重“道”和“德”的。“道”不干涉万物而使其顺其自然地完成生命的轮回。“道”生化万物，“德”蓄养万物，使其成长、成熟，并庇护万物。生化万物而不占为己有，恩泽万物而不自恃功高，主导万物而不做它们的主宰，这就是深奥玄妙的“德”啊！
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi explains why the Tao and virtue are esteemed and what is mystic virtue. The Tao gives birth to all things, while virtue nourishes them. If the Tao is the primordial source of generation, then virtue is the power that nurtures life after it comes into being. Apart from this, they also provided all things with the material conditions and external circumstances necessary for growth and completion. For this reason, there is nothing that does not honor the Tao and virtue. The Tao does not interfere with beings. It allow them to complete their cycles of life naturally. The Tao brings forth all things; virtue fosters, matures, and protects them. To create without possessing, to benefit without claiming merit, and to guide without dominating—this is the profound and subtle nature of mystic virtue.

title: 归元
original: 天下有始，以为天下母。既得其母，以知其子。既知其子，复守其母，没身不殆。塞其兑，闭其门，终身不勤。开其兑，济其事，终身不救。见其小曰明，守柔曰强。用其光，复归其明，无遗身殃。是为习常。
translation: There was a beginning of the universe, which can be regarded as the Mother of all things. If you know the origin, then you can know the children this Mother created: the myriad things. By knowing the children of this Mother and holding on to this Mother, you can stay away from dangers all your life. You will be free from troubles and harms if you can block the passageways and doors that will arouse your selfish desires. You will be beyond cure if you open the passageways and doors that will arouse your selfish desires and busy yourself with worldly affairs that will add to your distress. He who can perceive the subtle details in things is discerning; He who can maintain gentility possesses inner strength. He who can make use of the light of the Tao to restore his discernment incurs no disasters; This is called the eternal Tao.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子从哲学的高度探讨了对“道”的认识问题。老子说，“道”是宇宙万物的总根源，是天地万物的母体。“道”为母体，而由它产生的万物就是它的儿子。既然了解了万物的根源，也就认识万物本身了。了解了万物，再去固守万物的根本（即“道”），那么一个人终身也不会有危险了。老子接着警告世人，要阻塞嗜欲的孔窍和贪欲的心门，收敛欲望、破除妄念、内敛自省方能一生不受困扰；反之，烦恼会倍增，终身不可救药。能从细微处观察到具体事物的理就叫“明”，也就是“洞察力”；知道自己的强大，但能“守柔处下”就是“强”，也就是“自强不息”。运用“道”的智慧之光来恢复内在的明察秋毫的洞察力，就不会给自己惹来麻烦和灾难，这就是绵延不绝、用之不尽的“道”啊！在这里，老子不断地提醒世人要控制欲望，因为欲望越强烈，离悟道越远，越危险。“既知其子，复守其母，没身不殆”，面对红尘中的种种诱惑，一个人能坚守大道就会一生远离大灾大难。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi explores, from a philosophical perspective, what is Tao. He teaches that the Tao is the ultimate source of all things, the mother of heaven and earth. And all beings that arise from Tao are her children. To know the origin of things is therefore to understand things themselves. And having understood the myriad beings, if one holds fast to their root—the Tao—one will remain free from danger throughout life. Laozi further cautions that one must eliminate personal desires so that he can live without danger. Otherwise, one will live in all kinds of troubles and misery. To perceive the underlying principle though details is to have true insight. To know one’s strength yet abide in softness and humility is to have true strength. By applying the illuminating wisdom of the Tao to restore inner discernment, one avoids bringing  misfrtune upon oneself. This is the inexhaustible Tao. Laozi thus repeatedly reminds people to regulate selfish desires: the stronger one’s cravings, the farther one moves away from the path of Tao. As he teaches, “By knowing the children of this Mother and holding on to this Mother, you can stay away from dangers all your life.” Amid the temptations of the world, one who steadfastly abides in the Great Tao will remain far from grave disasters.

title: 益证
original: 使我介然有知，行於大道，唯施是畏。大道甚夷，而人好径。朝甚除，田甚芜，仓甚虚。服文彩，带利剑，厌饮食，财货有馀。是谓盗夸。非道也哉。
translation: If I were only slightly acquainted with the Tao, all that I would fear would be deviating from it. The road of the great Tao is very even, yet some rulers prefer by-paths. The ruling class goes against the Tao, which leads to the following grave consequences: The court becomes chaotic and corrupt; The fields go uncultivated and become barren; The granaries are very empty; The officials are still dressed luxuriantly; They wear ornamented swords; They eat and drink so excessively that they feel fed up with fine food and drink; They hoard and keep more wealth than necessary; This is indeed banditry. This does go against the Tao!
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子无情地揭露和鞭挞了统治阶级为满足自己的私欲，背离“道”强行而为，对人民横征暴敛，肆意妄为，过着骄奢淫逸的腐败生活。统治者不走平坦的大道，非要走歪门邪道。他们穿着华丽的衣服，腰间佩戴锋利的宝剑，吃腻了美味佳肴，搜刮百姓钱财而财货富足。朝廷腐败透顶，田地荒芜，粮仓空虚，而天下百姓则过着凄惨无比的生活。老子一针见血地指出，统治者的这种违背“道”的行为就是大盗行径，与盗匪无异！
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi exposes and condemns the ruling class for abandoning the Tao in pursuit of private desire. Acting against the Tao, they impose heavy taxes and upon the people while enjoying extravagant and corrupted life. Rather than following the broad and upright path, they choose crooked and deviant ways. They dress luxuriantly, wear sharp swords, and grow weary of delicacies while amass wealth by exploiting the people. This leads to serious consequences. The court becomes corrupted, the fields become barren and the granaries stand empty, while the common people live in misery. Laozi states that such conduct—so contrary to the Tao—is no different from bandits.

title: 修观
original: 善建者不拔。善抱者不脱。子孙以祭祀不辍。修之於身其德乃真。修之於家其德乃馀。修之於乡其德乃长。修之於邦其德乃丰。修之於天下其德乃普。故以身观身，以家观家，以乡观乡，以邦观邦，以天下观天下。吾何以知天下然哉？以此。
translation: One who follows the Tao is sure to make it; Therefore: What he has achieved cannot be easily uprooted; What he has been holding on to cannot be easily taken away; His virtue will benefit his descendants who will inherit and continue his virtue and honor him forever. If he cultivates himself by following the Tao, his virtue will be pure and genuine; If he cultivates his family by following the Tao, his virtue will be more than enough; If he cultivates his village by following the Tao, his virtue will e enduring;If he cultivates his country by following the Tao, his virtue will be abundant; If he cultivates his land by following the Tao, his virtue will be universal. Therefore: He can observe others by examining himself, other families by examining his own, other villages by examining his own, other countries by examining his own and other lands by examining his own. How do I get to know about the world? By means of the above-mentioned methods.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子重点论述了“善建”和“善抱”及其对于提升自身修养、治家、治乡、治国、治天下的积极作用。老子说，善于遵循“道”的规律做事的人（治国理政的君王）一旦有所建树，那么他所建树或成就的东西就不会被轻易拔除或废掉。善于坚持以“道”为行为标准的人一旦有所保持，他所坚持或保持的东西就不会被轻易夺走。如果君王能做到“善建”和“善抱”，那么他统治的国家就无亡国之虞。如果子孙能继承和遵守“善建”和“善抱”的道理，那么他的后代就会绵延不绝、生生不息。将此道理用于修身，那他的德行就会朴实纯真；将此道理用于治家，那他的德行就会泽及子孙，正所谓“积善之家必有余庆”；将此道理用于治乡，他的德行就会被更多人尊重，就会长久；将此道理用于治国，那么他的德行就会丰盛普及，恩泽众生；将此道理用于治天下，那么他的德行就会无限普及，人人尽享其恩泽。所以，人们可以通过自己的修身状况来了解他人，通过自家情况来了解别人家，以自己所居住的乡的情况了解别的乡，以自己所居住的国家的情况了解其他国家，以“善建”和“善抱”的道理为治理天下的标准来观察别人的天下。我是如何了解天下情况的呢？就是凭借以上的方法而得知的。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi focuses on the positive influence of a man who follows the Tao on himself, his family, his village, his country and the world. Laozi teaches that one who acts in accordance with the Tao—especially a ruler who governs by its principles—will establish achievements that cannot easily be uprooted. He will preserve what he holds, and it cannot easily be taken away. If a ruler can follow these two principles, his state will be sage and stable. If future generations inherit and follow these principles, then they will endure and flourish. When one cultivate himself with this principle, then his virtue will be simple and genuine. When applied to the family, his virtue will benefit future generations. That is why people say a virtuous family will enjoy lasting blessings. When applied to the community, his virtue earns enduring respect. When pplied to the country, his virtue becomes abundant and widely beneficent. When applied to the world, his virtue will benefit all under heaven. Therefore, one may understand others by examining oneself; understand other families by observing one’s own; understand other communities through one’s own community; understand other states through one’s own state; and observe the condition of the world by measuring it against the principles mentioned above. How, then, can I know the state of the world? By relying on these very methods.

title: 玄符
original: 含德之厚比於赤子。毒虫不螫，猛兽不据，攫鸟不抟。骨弱筋柔而握固。未知牝牡之合而全作，精之至也。终日号而不嗄，和之至也。知和曰常。知常曰明。益生曰祥。心使气曰强。物壮则老。谓之不道，不道早已。
translation: One who has abundant virtue is like a newly born baby. No poisonous insects and snakes sting him; No violent beasts attack him; No predatory birds prey on him. His bones and sinews are soft and tender, yet his grip is firm. He does not know the intercourse of male and female, yet his litle penis often rises; This means his vigor is strong to the full. He cries and screams all day long, yet his voice never becomes hoarse; This means his inner harmony reaches a perfect state. One who knows this harmony is in accord with the eternal Tao; To know the eternal Tao is to be enlightened; To lengthen one's life by over-nourishment is to incur disasters; To be swayed by one's impulsive desires is to display one's superiority. Things decline after they reach their prime; Being in prime goes against the Tao; Things that are not in accord with the Tao will soon perish.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子把德行厚重的人比喻成赤子。赤子的状态是“精之至”与“和之至”，前者指刚刚出生的婴儿精力充沛、元气饱满的状态，后者指婴儿的阴阳二气和谐状态达到了最佳。婴儿无知无欲、纯真无邪、精神饱满。婴儿没有任何攻击的意念和动作，在老子眼中简直就是“人畜无害”的存在！所以毒虫、猛兽、猛禽都不会伤害婴儿。婴儿虽不懂男女交合之事，但生殖器却坚挺，因其“精之至”。婴儿整天哭号，可嗓子却不沙哑，因其“和之至”。婴儿筋骨虽然柔弱，但小手的抓力却很牢固。能达到婴儿这种“原初”状态的人就是厚德之人， 而厚德之人就是与“道”同行的人或得“道”高人。在老子看来，能懂得“阴阳平衡”的人就是懂得自然规律的人；认识自然规律并懂得遵循自然规律的人就是明达之人。为了长寿过度补养生命就会破坏身体原有的和谐平衡，就一定会招来灾难。放纵争夺的欲望、好胜使气就是逞强好胜。事物达到鼎盛就会走向衰亡，这是违背了“道”的规律，不依“道”而行就会很快消亡。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi compares those with profound virtue to a newborn child. The state of the newborn represents the highest levels of vigor and harmony. The former refers to the infant’s vigorous vitality and abundant energy right after birth, while the latter points to the perfect balance of the yin and yang. A newborn is innocent, pure and free from desire. Without any aggressive intents or actions, he is truly a being of no malice. Thus, poisonous insects, fierce beasts, and predatory birds pose no threat to the infant. Though the child does not understand the act of reproduction, his penis often rises, as a result of this vital energy. The baby cries all day but its voice does not become hoarse, because of this perfect harmony. The infant’s muscles and bones may be weak, but the grip of its small hands is rather firm. Those who can return to this innocent state are the ones with great virtue. Such people understands and act in accordance with the Tao. For Laozi, those who understand the balance of yin and yang are those who comprehends the natural laws. To recognize these laws and follow them is to be wise. Excessive nourishment will destroy one’s inner harmony and balance, leading to disaster. Indulging in desires for power and victory is a form of arrogance. When things reach their peak, they inevitably decline, and being in prime go against the Tao. Those who do not follow the Tao will soon face their downfall.

title: 玄德
original: 知者不言。言者不知。挫其锐，解其纷，和其光，同其尘，是谓玄同。故不可得而亲。不可得而疏。不可得而利。不可得而害。不可得而贵。不可得而贱。故为天下贵。
translation: He who knows the Tao talks less about it; He who does not know the Tao talks more about it. He who knows the Tao blocks the passageways and doors of desires; He dulls his sharpness and eliminates entanglements; He conceals his brilliance and mixes with the worldly people; This is called profound and mystic identification. Such a sage is in no way touched by love or hatred, by gain or loss, and by honor or disgrace. Therefore, he is esteemed by all under Heaven.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子肯定了达到“玄同”境界的人就是懂“道”和依“道”而行的人，他们很少谈论“道”，是真正意义上的智者；而整天谈“道”的人其实是不懂“道”的人，这是没有智慧的表现。达到“玄同”境界的有道之人能做到如下：阻塞连接嗜欲的通道，关闭唤起嗜欲的门径，以达到无欲无求的境界；挫磨掉身上的锋芒与锐气，解除尘世的各种纷争，收敛身上的光耀，低调谦卑，混同于尘世，同流但不合污。这就是玄妙混沌的大同之道。对于进入这种状态的有道之人来说，他无私、无欲、谦下。因此，亲与疏、利与害、贵与贱等世俗观念都无法影响到他。所以，这种人会被天下人所敬仰与尊重。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi affirms that those who reach the state of “mystic identification with Tao” truly understand the Tao and live in accordance with it. They rarely speak about the Tao, for genuine wisdom does not parade itself in words. By contrast, those who constantly talk about the Tao do not truly understand it and lack real wisdom. Those who reach this state are able to block things that arouse personal desires, thereby have no desire. They soften their sharpness, dissolve worldly conflicts, temper their brilliance, and remain humble and unobtrusive. They move within the ordinary world, yet remaining unstained by it. This is the subtle and profound identification of the Tao. One who abides in such a state, is selfless, freed from desire, and humble. As a result, worldly things—closeness and distance, gain and loss, honor and disgrace—no longer exert influence. Such a person, therefore, is respected by all under heaven.

title: 淳风
original: 以正治国，以奇用兵，以无事取天下。吾何以知其然哉？以此。天下多忌讳而民弥贫。民多利器国家滋昏。人多伎巧奇物泫起。法令滋彰盗贼多有。故圣人云我无为而民自化。我好静而民自正。我无事而民自富。我无欲而民自朴。
translation: A ruler is on the right track if he governs the country by virtue of non-action, wages a war by means of crafty schemes and tricks, and wins the land through non- interference. How do I get to know it is the right way? I base my reason on the following points: The more prohibitions are issued, the poorer the people will become; The more sharp weapons the people possess, the more chaotic the country will become; The more cunning the people become, the more wickedness will arise in the country; The more laws and decrees are enacted, the more thieves and robbers there will be in the country. Therefore, as the sage put it: If I practice non-action, the people will cultivate themselves on their own; If I love tranquility, the people will naturally rectify themselves; If I do not meddle in their aff airs, the people will become prosperous; If I free myself from desires, the people will become simple and honest.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子突出强调了他的“无为而治”的治国理念，其核心思想是：“无为”、“好静”、“无事”和“无欲”。老子解释道：当君王妄为的时候，他治理天下就会出台越多的禁忌、法规、苛刻的规章制度等。令繁禁多，禁止做的事越多，老百姓就越不会安心生产，于是日子就越艰难；百姓手里的锋利武器越多（百姓的心智机巧越多），国家就越混乱；百姓崇尚奇巧与心智，那么奢靡之物和邪事怪事就会越来越多；君王颁布的法令繁多且多为严刑峻法，百姓不知所措以致民不聊生，盗贼就会越来越多。所以，老子引用圣人的话做总结：“我无为而民自化；我好静而民自正；我无事而民自富；我无欲而民自朴。”
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi highlights his principle of governing through non-action. It demands rulers to practice non-action and non-interference, to love tranquility and eliminate desires. A ruler should practice non-action, for the more he acts, the more prohibitions he imposes and the harder life becomes. His people should not be given too many weapons, for chaos will arise. The more cunning and intelligent his people become, the more wickedness emerges. He should not enact too many decrees, for they oppress the people and will lead to more crime. Therefore, Laozi concludes with the teaching of the sage: “If I practice non-action, the people will cultivate themselves on their own; If I love tranquility, the people will naturally rectify themselves; If I do not meddle in their affairs, the people will become prosperous; If I free myself from desires, the people will become simple and honest.

title: 顺化
original: 其政闷闷，其民淳淳。其政察察，其民缺缺。祸尚福之所倚。福尚祸之所伏。孰知其极，其无正。正复为奇，善复为妖。人之迷其日固久。是以圣人方而不割。廉而不刿。直而不肆。光而不耀。
translation: If a ruler practices non-action and non-interference, his people will become simple and honest; If a ruler governs his country by imposing harsh surveillance on his people, they will complain and become shrewd and cunning. W eal comes after woe; woe lies under weal. Who knows when one will turn into the other? There is no definite answer to this at all. The normal might change into the abnormal; The good might turn into the evil. The people have been long bewildered by this phenomenon. Therefore: The sage is square and impartial in his principles, but does not harm the people; He is thrifty and incorruptible, but not exacting; He is straightforward and candid, but not arrogant; He is brilliant, but does not overshadow others.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子论述了有关政治、社会及人生等方面的“福祸”相互转换的道理，该辩证哲学思想对中国文化影响深远。君王治国理政如果颁布的政令宽厚仁慈，体恤百姓疾苦，那么民众就会变得淳朴厚道；如果政令严厉苛刻，百姓就会抱怨，人民就会变得狡诈，民风就会颓废。灾祸就是福祉所依赖的东西（或产生幸福的原因），福祉就是灾祸所隐藏的地方。福祸转化的终极时刻在哪里呢？其实没有明确的标准或答案。正的会转变为邪的，善的会转变成恶的。这就是“反者，道之动”的道理。人们（统治阶级）迷惑于福祸转化的道理已经很久了。所以，有道的圣人（统治者）为人处世有棱角但不显得生硬；清正廉洁，但不伤人或苛求他人；直率坦诚，但不放肆无礼；才华突显，但光亮不耀眼。
commentaryEn: This chapter explains a key idea: the mutual transformation of fortune and misfortune in both politics, society and life. This dialectical insight has shaped Chinese culture. When a ruler governs with mercy and compassion for their his people, then his people will become honest and simple. On the contrary, when policies are harsh and oppressive, then resentment grows, people become cunning, and social morals decline. Misfortune is what fortune depends on; fortune is where misfortune is concealed. Blessing and disaster continually give rise to one another. But when exactly does one turn into the other? There is no fixed point. What seems right can become wrong; what appears good can turn into evil. This reflects the principle mentioned in chapter 40, that cycling is the movement of the Tao. For a long time, people—especially those in power—have been confused by this process of transformation. Therefore, the sage who truly understands the Tao is square but not rigid, frugal but not exacting, honest but not arrogant, and brilliant but dazzling.

title: 守道
original: 治人事天莫若啬。夫唯啬是谓早服。早服谓之重积德。重积德则无不克。无不克则莫知其极。莫知其极可以有国。有国之母可以长久。是谓深根固柢，长生久视之道。
translation: When it comes to governing the country and serving Heaven, no way proves better than practicing frugality . Only through frugality can an early preparation be made. An early preparation is equal to accumulating much virtue. With much virtue one is able to conquer all. With his all-conquering ability, his power is immeasurable. W ith his immeasurable power he is qualified to head a country. When he practices frugality as the foundation of governing his country, his governance will endure. This is indeed the Tao of "deep roots and sturdy stalks" by which a state can long survive in peace and prosperity.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子论述了治国理政的一个重要原则：“啬”，即“节俭”。“啬”不是“吝啬、抠门”的意思，而是“收敛欲望，节俭，积蓄、保养精力”等意思。只有节俭才是提前做准备的办法。这种早积蓄能量或提前做好准备的行为就是多积德。有了厚重的德行就没有战胜不了的事情。战无不胜就没有人知道他的能力极限，这样的人就可以成为一国之君了。有了治国的根本（节俭），国家就会长治久安。节俭就是国家巩固根基、绵延不绝、长久存在的根本方法。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi sets out a key principle of governance: “se”, often translated as frugality. This does not mean stinginess, but the disciplined curbing of desire and the conserving of resources. For Laozi, such restraint is the best form of preparation. To conserve early is to build strength in advance; this is what he calls the accumulation of de (virtue). With deep virtue, there is nothing one cannot overcome. When strength becomes inexhaustible, no one knows his boundaries and such a person is fit to rule a state. Thereofre, frugality is the foundation of a stable and sustainable governance.

title: 居位
original: 治大国若烹小鲜。以道莅天下，其迨ㄞ哄非其鬼不神，其神不伤人。非其神不伤人，圣人亦不伤人。夫两不相伤，故德交归焉。
translation: Governing a large country is like frying a small fish because it cannot be turned over too often. When he governs his country by following the Tao, the spirits will lose their supernatural power. It is not that they lose their power, but that their potential power fails to harm the people. Neither the spirits nor the sage can harm the people. They both fail to harm the people, and a harmonious society will emerge in which the people live peacefully and prosperously, basking in the sunshine of virtue.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子提出了“治大国若烹小鲜”的著名比喻。老子把治理大国比喻为烹调小鱼。小鱼肉鲜嫩，若在烹制过程中不停地翻动，那么小鱼就会碎掉。老子在暗示统治者在治国理政的过程中要行“无言之教”和“无为之治”。政令繁多，会令百姓不知所措；朝令夕改，会令百姓无所适从。遵循“道”来治理天下，鬼神就会失去作怪的能力；并不是鬼神失去了伤害人的能力，而是其能力伤害不到人；不仅鬼神不伤害人，有道的圣人（统治者）也不伤害人。有道的圣人依“道”治理天下，邪恶的人（鬼神）就能被制服，也就不敢出来伤害或干扰百姓了，百姓就受到“德”的恩泽了，就可以按自己的本性悠然生活了
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi introduces his famous metaphor: “Governing a large country is like frying a small fish.” A small fish would fall apart if you stir it too often. Through this image, Laozi cautions rulers against excessive interference and advocates governance through restraint—teaching without preaching and acting without overmanaging. When policies are too numerous, people grow confused; when orders change too often, they lose their sense of direction. Governing in accordance with the Tao minimizes such disruption. Under such rule, even disruptive forces—symbolized by spirits and demons—lose their power to cause harm. It is not that their power disappears, but that it no longer reaches the people. Likewise, a ruler who follows the Tao does not harm the people. When governance aligns with the Tao, destructive forces are subdued, social disorder recedes, and the people come to live under the quiet protection of de (virtue), free to follow their own nature in peace.

title: 谦德
original: 大国者下流，天下之交。天下之牝。牝常以静胜牡。以静为下。故大国以下小国，则取小国。小国以下大国，则取大国。故或下以取，或下而取。大国不过欲兼畜人。小国不过欲入事人。夫两者各得所欲，大者宜为下。
translation: A great country should choose to stay in lowliness, playing the role of a female and functioning as a confluence of rivers. The female always wins over the male by virtue of tranquility in that the former chooses to take the lower position. Therefore: If a great country humbles itself before a small country, it will win the allegiance of the latter; If a small country humbles itself before a great country, it will win the trust and protection of the latter. The case is either the former or the latter. What a great country needs is nothing but the allegiance of a small country; What a small country needs is no more than the protection of a great country. In this way, they both gain what they desire; In their interactions, the great country should take particular care to behave humbly before the small country.
commentaryZh:
本章体现了老子关于大国如何以“谦下”及“卑下”的雌柔态度对待小国的外交思想，即“善下”。在老子看来，大国应该像处于江河下游那样，保持雌柔处下的姿态以充当天下如支流般汇入的、小国的交汇之地，即大国要拥有海纳百川的胸怀和包容的气魄。因为，雌性能以其宁静制服雄性的刚猛。雌性喜安静而能处下位。所以，大国如果能以谦虚卑下的态度对待小国，那么就会赢得小国的信任和依附。小国若能以谦虚卑下的态度对待大国，就会获得大国的信任与支持。因此，不管是大国还是小国，都有同样的最终目的：大国无非是想兼并
与保护小国，而小国无非是想依附大国以得到庇护。因为大国与小国都以谦虚卑下的态度对待彼此，所以能满足各自的需求与愿望，在国与国的交往中，大国更要谦卑处下位。
commentaryEn: This chapter articulates Laozi’s vision of diplomacy, especially how a great state should relate to smaller ones through humility and play the role of female, that is to be “willing to take the lower position.” A great power should be like the lower reaches of a river: by remaining low and receptive, it becomes the place where all tributaries converge. That is a great country should be wide and inclusive. Laozi associates this posture with the feminine principle: quiet and willing to stay in lowly places. It overcomes the male not by confrontation but by stillness and patience. When a great state approaches smaller states with humility, it earns their trust and allegiance. Likewise, when smaller states act with modesty toward greater ones, they gain protection and support. Ultimately, both large and small states seek fulfillment of their needs—the great state seeks to unite and safeguard, while the small state seeks security through affiliation. Mutual humility allows both aims to be realized. For Laozi, it is the great power that must particularly learn to behave humbly.

title: 为道
original: 道者万物之奥。善人之宝，不善人之所保。美言可以市尊。美行可以加人。人之不善，何弃之有。故立天子、置三公，虽有拱璧以先驷马，不如坐进此道。古之所以贵此道者何。不曰∶求以得，有罪以免邪？故为天下贵。
translation: The Tao is the creator of the universe; It is cherished and valued alike by those who follow the Tao and those who do not follow the Tao. With the Tao, well-said words can win the respect of others, and good deeds can influence others and win their admiration. Why would the Tao forsake those who do not follow it? Therefore: On crowning the emperor and appointing the Three Ministers, it would be better to present the emperor the Tao than a large jade disk followed by a team of four horses. Why did the ancients so prize the Tao? As they put it, "If one followed the Tao, he could get what he desired, and his transgressions would be pardoned. " That's why the Tao is held so dear under Heaven.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子论述了“道”是万事万物的主导和庇护所。在“道”面前世人皆平等，这突出了“道”对人类精神文明建设的重要意义。“道”既是善人（依“道” 而行之人）的珍宝，也是不善之人（不依“道”而行之人）的护身法宝。美好的言辞（依“道”而行之人的言语）可以换来别人的尊重，（依“道”而行之人）高尚的品行可以让自己受到重视。不善的人不会被“道”抛弃，即世人在“道”面前一律平 等。所以国家在拥立天子和设置三公的时候，虽有献拱璧在先、献驷马在后的仪式，还不如把“无为而治”的“道”献给他们。从古至今，人们为何珍视“道”呢？ 不就是说求“道”就可以得到它的帮助，犯罪的人也可以得到“道”的宽恕吗？正因如此，“道”才被天下人珍视。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi presents the Tao as the ultimate ground and refuge of all things. Before the Tao, all humanbeings are equal, which underscores its significance for people’s spiritual and moral life. The Tao is a treasure for both those who live in accord with it and those who do not. Words spoken in harmony with the Tao earn respect, and conduct shaped by it brings people’s admiration. Yet the Tao does not abandon those who do not follow it; it remains open to all without discrimination. For this reason, when crowning the emperor and appoints high ministers, no ritual offerings, however precious, can compare to presenting them with the principle of governing through non-action. Why has the Tao been cherished throughout history? Because those who follow it find support, and even those who have erred may find mercy through it. That’s why the Tao is held so dear by the world.

title: 恩始
original: 为无为，事无事，味无味。大小多少，报怨以德。图难於其易，为大於其细。天下难事必作於易。天下大事必作於细。是以圣人终不为大，故能成其大。夫轻诺必寡信。多易必多难。是以圣人犹难之，故终无难矣。
translation: A ruler who follows the Tao governs his country through non-action, manages his people' s affairs through non-interference and conducts his governance naturally without personal desires. The big comes from the small, and much is accumulated from little; Hatred can be dissolved through virtue. A difficult thing can be tackled by dealing with its easy aspects; A great task can be fulfilled by dealing with its insignificant aspects. Put it another way, when one copes with the most difficult things in the world, he must start from their easy aspects; when one handles the greatest tasks in the world, he must begin with their details. Therefore: The sage never attempts to accomplish great things from the start, which enables him to achieve greatness in the end. He who makes promises lightly seldom fulfills them; The easier one takes things to be, the harder they will turn out to be. The sage never encounters difficulties in that he always deems things difficult.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子开宗明义地提出“为无为，事无事，味无味”，即“无为而无不 为”的哲学思想。老子指出，在此思想指导下，不管人们要做成难事还是大事， 都要先从小处、细处、易处着手，由小到大、由少到多、由易到难，一步一个脚印， 最终实现从量变到质变的飞跃。所以，有道的圣人（统治者）从不好大喜功、贪大而忽略细节，最终能成就大业。老子接着以强逻辑的口吻下结论说：轻易承 诺的人一定缺乏诚信；把事情看得太容易就一定会遇到很多困难。有道的圣人 总是把事情看得很难，所以自始至终也不会遇到难题。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi sets out his core principle at the very beginning: “govern through non-action, manage people’s affairs through non-interference and conducts governance without personal desires.”  This encapsulates his philosophy of “non-action that leaves nothing undone.” Guided by this principle, Laozi argues that whether one aims to accomplish difficult tasks or great undertakings, he should begin with what is small, simple, and manageable. Progress step by step—from the minor to the major, from the few to the many, from the easy to the hard—until gradual accumulation leads to decisive transformation. For this reason, the sage or ruler who follows Tao never seeks quick or great success at the expense of details, and thereby enables lasting achievement. Laozi then draws two sharp conclusions: those who make promises lightly lack trustworthiness, and those who treat matters as easy will inevitably encounter hardship. The sage, by contrast, approaches everything with seriousness and caution and therefore always conquers challenges.

title: 守微
original: 其安易持，其未兆易谋。其脆易泮，其微易散。为之於未有，治之於未乱。合抱之木生於毫末。九层之台起於累土。千里之行始於足下。为者败之，执者失之。是以圣人无为故无败，无执故无失。民之从事常於几成而败之。慎终如始则无败事。是以圣人欲不欲，不贵难得之货。学不学，复众人之所过，以辅万物之自然而不敢为。
translation: It is easy to control a stable situation; It is easy to handle a thing that has not yet shown ill omens; A brittle thing is easily broken; A tiny thing is easily dissolved. It is better to nip something unpleasant in the bud before it happens; It is better to eradicate disorder before it erupts. A huge tree springs up from a tiny sprout; A nine-storied tower begins with a pile of earth; A long journey starts with a single step. He who goes against the Tao fails; He who acts willfully to fulfill his desires loses whatever he thirsts for. Therefore: The sage acts in accord with the Tao, and he never fails; He never attempts to fulfil his personal desires, and he never loses anything. This always happens when people engage in doing things; They usually fail at the very moment when they come close to their final success. If one can be as cautious at the end as he was at the start, he will never fail. Therefore: The sage desires what others do not thirst for; He does not prize rare goods; He learns what others hate to learn; He practices non-action with a view to compensating for people' s faults and helping the myriad things grow naturally; He acts in accord with the Tao, avoiding any interference in their natural growth.
commentaryZh: 本章是《道德经》中非常有名的一章。老子在本章中论述了任何事物都是从幼小发展到壮大的一个从量变到质变的过程。认识事物发展的规律就是按客观规律办事的尊“道”行为。“居安思危”（其安易持）和“防患于未然”（治之于未乱）的哲学思想就来自老子的这一章。老子用“合抱之木，生于毫末；九层之台，起于累土；千里之行，始于足下”这警句般的语言来阐释事物发展由小到大的过程。荀子的“不积跬步，无以至千里；不积小流，无以成江海”与其内核相 通。违背“道”的行为就会失败，一心为私利而为就会失去所有。有道的圣人 （统治者）依“道”而行“无为之治”，所以不会失败，无私无欲不执着于个人私欲， 也不会失去什么。人们做事常常在开始的时候非常谨慎，但往往就在要成功的时候失败了，正所谓“行百里者半九十”或“功败垂成”。如果对待事情从头至尾一样慎重认真，而不是虎头蛇尾，就不会遭遇失败了。有道的圣人渴望别人所不向往的东西，不看重那些难得的珍稀贵重之物；他学习众人不学的东西（道），用以补救众人所犯的过失，来辅助天下万物能按“道”的规律自然成长和发展而不加以人为干涉。
commentaryEn: This is one of the most celebrated chapters of Tao Te Ching. Laozi observes that all things grow from the small to the great through gradual accumulation, until quantitative change gives rise to qualitative transformation. To recognize this pattern is to act in harmony with the Tao—by respecting natural processes rather than forcing results. From this chapter come ideas such as staying vigilant in times of stability and addressing problems before they take shape. Laozi illustrates this principle with vivid images: a towering tree that begins as a tiny shoot, a high terrace built from layers of earth, and a long journey that starts with a single step. Xunzi, a philosopher in the Warring States Period expresses the same idea––Without accumulating small steps, one cannot reach a thousand miles. Actions that run against the Tao are destined to fail, and those driven solely by self-interest ultimately lose everything. By contrast, the sage or a ruler who follows the Tao—governs through non-action and thus avoids failure. Free from selfish desire, he has nothing to lose. Laozi also notes a common human failing: people are often careful at the beginning of an endeavor, only to falter when success is within reach. If one remains as attentive at the end as at the start, failure can be avoided. The sage values what others overlook, rejects rare luxuries, and learns what others neglect—the Tao itself. In doing so, he helps correct human errors and allows all things to grow according to their own nature, without interference.

title: 淳德
original: 古之善为道者，非以明民，将以愚之。民之难治，以其智多。故以智治国，国之贼。不以智治国，国之福。知此两者，亦稽式。常知稽式，是谓玄德。玄德深矣、远矣！与物反矣。然後乃至大顺。
translation: The ancient rulers who knew how to act in accord with the Tao in their governance did not attempt to make their people intelligent and cunning; Instead, they spared no efforts to make them simple and honest. The reason why it is hard to govern the people is that they are too intelligent and cunning. Therefore: It will incur disasters if a ruler governs his country through cunning measures; It will be a blessing if a ruler governs his country not through cunning measures. As for a ruler, the difference between the above two measures proves a crucial principle to be kept in his governance. To know this principle is called the mystic and subtle virtue. This virtue is profound, far-reaching and omnipresent, operating in the direction contrary to the myriad things, but in accord with the Tao; It will finally bring the people to grand harmony and peace.
commentaryZh: 本章是老子《道德经》中最容易被误解的章节之一。很多人认为老子在提倡“愚民”的治国之策，其实老子的“愚民”并非使人民或百姓无知、愚蠢，而是使他们不要追求所谓的“智巧、心机、智谋、算计”等来钩心斗角、尔虞我诈以达到自己私利最大化的目的。在老子看来，真正有道的统治者不应用智巧来使人民变得狡诈、奸猾，而是依“道”而治以使百姓剔除巧智与奸猾回归敦厚朴实的为人之道。老百姓之所以难管理就是巧智太多，容易钻法令的空子。所以，用智巧来治国，那就是国家的灾难；反之，就是国家的福祉了。能知道二者的差别就是接近“道”的法则。了解这个法则就是深奥玄妙的“德”。这深奥玄妙的“德”遥不可及，与人们的认知正好相反，但持守此“德”就是与“道”相合，最终天下会达到最大程度的和顺、太平、安定。
commentaryEn: This chapter is among the most widely misunderstood in Tao Te Ching. It is misinterprets as obscurantism, but this misses Laozi’s intent. By urging rulers to “make the people simple and honest”, Laozi is not advocating ignorance. Rather, he cautions against excessive cleverness, cunning knowledge, and the relentless pursuit of private gain. For Laozi, an enlightened ruler does not govern by encouraging cunning or calculation. He governs in accordance with the Tao, allowing people to return naturally to honesty and simplicity. People become difficult to govern precisely because excessive cleverness enables them to exploit loopholes in laws and regulations. Rule by clever devices invites disorder; rule by simplicity brings good fortune. To recognize the difference between these two approaches is to glimpse the principle of the Tao. To live by it is to embody a subtle and profound virtue—one that runs against common assumptions yet aligns fully with the natural order. When such virtue prevails, harmony, peace, and lasting stability arise naturally.

title: 后己
original: 江海之所以能为百谷王者，以其善下之，故能为百谷王。是以圣人欲上民，必以言下之。欲先民，必以身後之。是以圣人处上而民不重，处前而民不害。是以天下乐推而不厌。以其不争，故天下莫能与之争。
translation: The great rivers and seas can be the confluence of all the streams in that they humbly choose to stay below them. To head the people, a sage must speak humbly before them; To guide the people, he must put his interests behind theirs. Therefore: The people do not feel overburdened even if the sage stays above them; They do not feel harmed even if the sage remains ahead of them. In this way the people under Heaven are wiling to support and esteem him.No one in the world can contend with him in that he does not contend with anyone at all.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子着重论述了有道的统治者在治国理政过程中要实施“无为而治”和“不争之争”的策略。这样国家方能太平和谐，这样的君王也会受到百姓的爱戴拥护，而且天下无人能与他相争。老子比喻说：江海之所以能成为百川的汇集之地，是因为它心甘情愿处在最低处以纳百川之溪流。所以，有道的圣人要想位居人民之上就要在言辞上对百姓谦和卑下；要想领导人民就要把自己的利益放于人民之后，即不与民争利。所以，这样的君王即使位居百姓之上（处于领导地位），百姓也不感到负担沉重；居前领导人民，百姓也不感到利益受到伤害。所以，百姓愿意推举、拥戴这样的君王而不感到厌倦。因为他不争，所以天下没有人能争得过他。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi emphasizes that a ruler who follows the Tao should govern through non-action and non-contention. Only in this way can a state remain peaceful and harmonious, and only such a ruler can win the genuine support of the people, with no rival under Heaven. Laozi illustrates this with the image of rivers flowing into the sea: the sea becomes the gathering place of all waters precisely because it willingly stays at the lowest point. Likewise, a ruler who wishes to stand above the people must speak with humility, and one who seeks to lead them must place the people’s interests before his own. In this way, people never feel repressed or their interests harmed. They therefore support such a ruler willingly and without resentment. Precisely because he does not contend, no one in the world can contend with him.

title: 三宝
original: 天下皆谓我道大似不肖。夫唯大故似不肖。若肖，久矣！其细也夫。我有三宝持而保之∶一曰慈， 二曰俭，三曰不敢为天下先。慈故能勇，俭故能广，不敢为天下先故能成器长。今舍慈且勇，舍俭且广，舍後且先，死矣！夫慈以战则胜，以守则固。天将救之以慈卫之。
translation: The whole world claims that my Tao is so great that it fails to resemble anything concrete. It fails to resemble anything concrete in that it is so great. If it did resemble something concrete, it would have long been categorized and studied in detail, and if that is the case, it will become petty and insignificant! I have three treasures I hold dear and protect: The first is mercy; The second is frugality; The third is humility or the unwillingness to be the first. With mercy, one will become brave; With frugality, one will enjoy a sustainable development; With humility or the unwillingness to be the first, one will be qualified to act as a leader. Therefore: If one deserts mercy but keeps courage, frugality but continues expansion and the unwillingness to be the first but takes the lead, he is doomed to failure. Mercy enables one to be victorious in attack and well-grounded in defense. If Heaven is about to save someone, it guards him with mercy.
commentaryZh: 本章是《道德经》中非常著名的一章。在本章中，老子把大家都觉得很抽象 的“道”概括为三个特征，即“三宝”：慈、俭、不敢为天下先。同时，老子也论述了 “三宝”的各自作用及违反“三宝”原则会带来的恶果等。在“三宝”中，老子特别 突出了“慈”为宝中之宝。
commentaryEn: This is one of the most celebrated chapters of Tao Te Ching. Here, Laozi distills the otherwise abstract notion of the Tao into three defining qualities, known as the “Three Treasures”: mercy, frugality, and humility. He explains the function of each treasure and warns that when these principles are ignored, one is doomed to failure. Among the three, Laozi places particular emphasis on mercy, regarding it as the most essential of all.

title: 配天
original: 善为士者不武。善战者不怒。善胜敌者不与。善用人者为之下。是谓不争之德。是谓用人之力。是谓配天之极。
translation: A good general does not resort to violence impulsively. A good fighter does not burst into anger easily. A good conqueror does not turn to hostile confrontations frequently but subdues his enemy without tough battles. A man who excels at utilizing people often humbles himself before them. This is the virtue of non-contention and the ability of making use of others' strength as well; This virtue is in accord with the Tao of Heaven, which has proven to be the highest criterion from the ancient times.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子阐释了他的军事思想：“不武、不怒、不与、不争”。老子认为善于为将帅的人不崇尚武力、不轻言战争；善于用兵的人不会轻易动怒、轻率冲动；善于战胜敌人的人常常不会与敌人正面对抗，而是能“不战而屈人之兵”；善于用人的人（善于领导军队打仗的人）能谦虚卑下地对待他人（兵将）。这是不争强好胜的“德”，是会用人的能力表现（即借力打力的能力或用兵之道），这样德才兼备就符合天道了，是自古流传下来（用兵打仗）的最高准则和标准。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi articulates his military philosophy through four principles: not relying on violence, not acting in anger, not confronting head-on, and not contending for dominance. He argues that a capable general does not resort to violence impulsively; a skilled fighter remains calm and never acts out of rage or impulse; a good conqueror avoids hostile confrontations, achieving victory without battle. Likewise, a leader who knows how to employ others treats subordinates with humility rather than arrogance. This is the virtue of non-contention—the ability to lead, to draw on the strength of others, and to prevail without coercion. When moral character and strategic skill are combined in this way, they accord with the Tao. Laozi presents this as the highest principle of warfare, handed down through the ages.

title: 玄用
original: 用兵有言，吾不敢为主而为客。不敢进寸而退尺。是谓行无行。攘无臂。扔无敌。执无兵。祸莫大於轻敌。轻敌几丧吾宝。故抗兵相加哀者胜矣。
translation: As a saying for warfare goes, "I dare not to attack first and instead set up adefense. I dare not to advance an inch and instead retreat a foot." This means that much as you have got the formation ready, you should leave the impression that you have no formation; This means that much as you intend to raise your arms, you should make it appear that you have no arms to lift; This means that much as you have weapons, you should give the impression that you have no weapons to hold; This means that much as you are encountering your enemy, you should make it appear that you have no enemy to fight against. Underestimating the enemy is the greatest disaster; Underestimating the enemy nearly amounts to losing the three treasures. Therefore: If two equally matched armies are at war, the sorrow-laden side often gets the upper hand in the end.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子借他人的话阐释了自己以退为进的辩证军事哲学思想。老 子提出不主动发动战争、以退为进、以守为攻、骄兵必败、哀兵必胜等军事思 想。毛泽东的《论持久战》中关于中国抗日战争的概括性论述“退却、相持、进 攻”的核心思想就折射了老子这一章的军事思想。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi articulates, through the words of others, his own dialectical philosophy of warfare, emphasizing the strategic principle of advancing by yielding. Laozi advocates several military principles: not initiating hostilities, advancing through retreat, defending in order to counterattack, that an arrogant army is destined for defeat, and that a grieving or resolute army is likely to prevail. The core strategic sequence of “retreat, stalemate, and counteroffensive” outlined by Mao Zedong in the book On Protracted War, which summarizes the course of China’s resistance during the War of Resistance against Japan, can be seen as reflecting a strategic logic comparable to the military thought expressed in this chapter.

title: 知难
original: 吾言甚易知、甚易行。天下莫能知、莫能行。言有宗、事有君。夫唯无知，是以我不知。知我者希，则我者贵。是以圣被褐怀玉。
translation: It is fairly easy to make sense of my teachings and put them into practice. But rulers fail to understand and practice them in that they are blinded by their selfish desires. My teachings and actions are based on the Tao. It is because they fail to comprehend my teachings and actions that they do not catch me. There are few rulers who can understand me and even fewer rulers who can follow my advice concerning governance. That's why the sage wears coarse clothes with a precious jade (the Tao) hidden in his bosom.
commentaryZh: 在本章中，老子把自己喻为“道”本身，抒发了自己的治国之道被君王厌弃而产生的郁闷之情。老子说他的治国之道是很容易被了解和被践行的，可天下的君王就是不了解、不去践行。老子说他的治国理政的言论和行事都是有根基的，那个根基就是“道”。天下君王因为不了解治国之道，所以不了解他的主张。老子说：“了解我的人很少，能以我的主张作为行为准则的人更难能可贵了。”所以有道的圣人像穷苦人一样穿着粗布麻衣，但怀揣着珍贵的宝玉，即治国之道。
commentaryEn: In this chapter, Laozi likens himself to the Tao, expressing his frustration that rulers fail to understand and practice his principles of governance. He emphasizes that his approach to ruling is simple to understand and follow, yet rulers all fail to grasp or implement it. Laozi insists that his teachings and actions are grounded in the Tao—but because rulers do not understand this Tao, they fail to appreciate his guidance. As he notes, “Few truly understand me, and even fewer follow my teachings as a guide for action.” For this reason, sage resembles a poor man, wearing coarse  clothes, yet carrying within him a priceless jade—the Tao. In this chapter, Laozi draws on the words of others to articulate his dialectical philosophy of warfare, one that advances by retreating. He argues against initiating war, advocating strategic withdrawal, defense as a form of offense, and the principles that arrogance leads to defeat while compassion and restraint lead to victory. These ideas find a clear echo in Mao Zedong’s On Protracted War, in which Mao presents the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression as unfolding in three phases: strategic retreat, strategic stalemate, and strategic counteroffensive.

title: 知病
original: 知不知上，不知知病。夫唯病病，是以不病。圣人不病，以其病病。夫唯病病，是以不病。
